subject: Re: BlueChip MAP — consolidation, compressed eval cadence, and contingency runbook
messages:
From: Sophie Ramos <sophie.ramos@bluechip.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brian Lee <brian.lee@bluechip.io>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Updated MAP & slight tweak to eval window

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Attached is an updated mutual action plan (MAP) reflecting the outcomes from the session. Two items to flag: procurement needs an extra week to route the PO internally, and our security team asked for an additional short eval focused on data residency (two small tests). Both are likely to shift the original close date by ~10 business days unless we compress the evaluation cadence.

Could Redwood propose a compressed/evidence-first eval runbook we can agree to? We want to keep momentum.

Attachments: BlueChip_MAP_v1.2.pdf, MAP_Change_Log.xlsx

— Sophie Ramos
Head of Platform Partnerships
BlueChip Technologies

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Ramos <sophie.ramos@bluechip.io>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Updated MAP & slight tweak to eval window

Sophie — thanks for the MAP and the heads-up on procurement. High level: we can compress the eval cadence and add a short data-residency test as a gated milestone, but we need alignment on two levers to avoid slip:

1) A single PO routing cutoff (we'll treat approvals after X date as procurement-late trigger)
2) Permission to run a short Dedicated trial (3 days) for the residency tests — this reduces iteration time vs. hosted throttles.

I'll loop Jonas (pilot/resourcing) and Laura (delivery lead) to draft a compact runbook and an updated risk log. If procurement is still delayed past the cutoff we should escalate to execs for a prioritized PO lane.

Next steps: Jonas/Laura — can you draft the compressed-eval runbook and a one-page risk log by EOD tomorrow? Sophie/Brian — can you confirm the PO routing timeline and the interlock for a 3-day dedicated trial?

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, North America Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Brian Lee <brian.lee@bluechip.io>
To: Sophie Ramos <sophie.ramos@bluechip.io>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Updated MAP & slight tweak to eval window

Hannah/Sophie — quick procurement note: finance has a scheduled vendor review on Tue 4/16 and then an approvals batch on Fri 4/19. Realistically the earliest PO will be cut is 4/22 — so that is ~9 business days from today. If we need a Softer deadline for your escalation gate, use 4/18.

I'll keep you posted if we can fast-track, but current estimate is PO week of 4/22.

— Brian
Senior Procurement Analyst
BlueChip Technologies

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2029 07:40:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: compressed-eval runbook & mitigations (internal)

Hannah/Laura — attaching an internal draft (summarized below) for the compressed evaluation cadence and mitigations so we can send a clean version to BlueChip: 

Summary draft (short):
- Goal: Keep close within original quarter by compressing evals and adding contingency tests to MAP.
- Change: Move full eval window from 10 business days to 5 business days using parallel tests:
  * Day 1–2: Deployment + smoke + residency check (dedicated 3-day trial)
  * Day 3: Latency/cost profiling with sample traffic
  * Day 4: Functionality/fuzz and policy checks
  * Day 5: Final report + signoffs (security, platform, procurement ack)
- Mitigations: Prefix caching enabled, priority routing on trial, and we’ll offer a 30% token-credit buffer if BlueChip needs more run-time due to procurement hold.
- Risk register entries (top 3):
  1) Procurement delay beyond 4/18 -> Exec escalation required
  2) Residency test fails -> fallback to staged deployment (longer runway)
  3) Data access policy delays -> require PO window extension

If this looks good I'll refine language and create the one-page risk log and the MAP change note for Sophie.

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Ramos <sophie.ramos@bluechip.io>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2029 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: compressed-eval runbook & mitigations

On Fri, Apr 12, 2029 at 07:40, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hannah/Laura — attaching an internal draft (summarized below) for the compressed evaluation cadence and mitigations so we can send a clean version...

Thanks Jonas — I updated the mitigation language and added two operational gates: (A) Dedicated trial approval (ops checklist) and (B) Security signoff checkpoint at end of Day 3.

Sophie/Brian — attaching a version of the MAP that reflects these gates and the compressed cadence. Note the contingency clause that if PO is not signed by 2029-04-18 we will: (1) enact exec escalation and (2) provision a temporary hosted smoke window (reduced guarantees) to allow limited production testing while the PO routes.

Attachment: Statement_of_Work_v3.docx (SOW forward for signature), BlueChip_MAP_v1.2.pdf

Please confirm acceptance of the gating language and whether your security team can commit the Day 3 signoff window. If yes, we'll prepare a DocuSign packet for the SOW and a one-page risk log.

— Laura
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Ramos <sophie.ramos@bluechip.io>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brian Lee <brian.lee@bluechip.io>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: compressed-eval runbook & mitigations

Laura/Hannah — appreciated. We can commit to the Day 3 security checkpoint provided the residency tests complete on Day 1–2 and we have the detailed acceptance criteria for the residency test (hashing, region logs, KMS call traces). I'll review the SOW and expect to sign via DocuSign if procurement keeps to the 4/22 window.

One ask: please include an explicit executive escalation contact and target dates in the runbook if procurement is delayed beyond 4/18. That makes internal gating easier for my stakeholders.

— Sophie

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Ramos <sophie.ramos@bluechip.io>, Brian Lee <brian.lee@bluechip.io>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: FINAL: Consolidated runbook, re-baselined close, and escalation path

Sophie/Brian — thanks for the confirmations. Attached is the consolidated runbook and the one-page risk log. Key outcomes and new baselines below (formal MAP update attached):

- Re-baselined close target: 2029-04-26 (previous target: 2029-04-18). This accounts for PO earliest cut of 4/22 and gives three business days post-PO for provisioning and final sign-off.
- Compressed eval cadence (5 business days) accepted — Days 1–2 residency + smoke, Day 3 security signoff, Day 4 profiling, Day 5 final report.
- Escalation gate: if PO not signed by 2029-04-18 -> Exec escalation to Redwood SVP of Sales (Marcus Lin) and BlueChip VP of Finance (Sophie loop to her exec). Marcus is authorized to approve a temporary credit buffer and priority capacity to keep the close on track.
- Contingency: If residency test fails, fallback to staged deployment; expected impact: +7 business days.

Related links: HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood/contacts/bluechip/1173, DocuSign: https://docusign.com/prepare/BLUE-INV-2029-1173
Attachments: BlueChip_MAP_v1.2.pdf, Statement_of_Work_v3.docx, MAP_Change_Log.xlsx

I'll prepare the DocuSign envelope for SOW and a short exec escalation note that the account team and BlueChip can use if procurement misses 4/18. Please confirm by EOD tomorrow and we'll spin up the Dedicated trial slot for 4/23 if PO clears.

— Hannah Schmitt
Director, North America Sales
Redwood Inference
